html:
Ujamaa, Swahili for familyhood, was the African socialism of Julius Nyerere, set out in the Arusha Declaration of 1967, which shaped Tanzania until the mid 1980s.

Its centre was the village. From 1973 to 1976 the government moved millions of rural people, often by force, into planned villages, so that services could reach them and farming could be shared. Banks and firms were nationalised.

Farm output fell and the economy struggled, and Tanzania turned to market reforms after Nyerere stepped down in 1985. Yet ujamaa, with schooling in Swahili, gave Tanzania a strong national identity and few of the ethnic conflicts of its neighbours.
sum: Ujamaa, Swahili for familyhood, was the African socialism of Julius Nyerere, set out in the Arusha Declaration of 1967, which shaped Tanzania until the mid 1980s.
